transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (CTO - Hightower), Liam O'Neill (ML Eng), Sara Gomez (Data Privacy)

Summary (auto):
Customer exploring model selection across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Key concerns: long context support (up to 100k tokens), multilingual quality, tool-calling (external tool invocation and structured outputs), and compliance (SOC 2, KMS, VPC). They want benchmark runs and TCO comparison.

Topics: Model families (Llama/Redwood-verifieds, Mistral-ish, Claude-ish variants), quantization/throughput, context length, multilingual evals, tool calling APIs, deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), security & audit requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the platform team at Redwood. Diego is our solutions engineer. Priya, do you want to intro real quick?
[00:08] Priya (Hightower CTO): Yeah hi, Priya here. We're evaluating inference options for our customer-facing assistant. Main things: long context—like 50k to 100k tokens for multi-doc summarization, multilingual support across EN/ES/FR/DE/JP, and ability to call internal tools securely. Sara is here for compliance.
[00:22] Sara (Data Privacy): Hi. I'll mostly listen but will ask on data residency, audit logs and KMS.
[00:26] Diego (Redwood SE): Cool, great. Quick agenda: baseline on current stack, performance targets, what "tool calling" means for you, and then model tradeoffs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[00:33] Liam (ML Eng): We're currently running a mix of OpenAI for quick experiments and some in-house fine-tuned models on GCP. Costs are spiking with our 100k context experiments; also latency is all over the place.
[00:44] Priya: Timeline is tight — pilot in 6 weeks ideally. Stakeholders: product, infra, legal. Success = sub-2s generation latency for short-turn queries, and <5s average for long-context summarize flows; quality parity or better than our current tuned Llama-variant (we call it "Llama-fork").
[00:58] Maya: Great. Can I ask about peak QPS and batching tolerance?
[01:02] Liam: Peak QPS around 30 req/s for active regions, but most requests are heavy — long context - so throughput is different. Batching fine if latency SLOs hold.
[01:12] Diego: Understood. Quick note on terms — our "Hosted" offering is Redwood API with model catalog; "Dedicated" is reserved GPU pools you can control for predictable throughput; "Private" puts control plane in your VPC or on-prem. Each has different tradeoffs for latency, cost, and data residency.
[01:27] Priya: On model selection: we're interested in open models. We saw Redwood's catalog has optimized variants. How do you recommend picking?
[01:33] Diego: Good question. There are a few axes: context-length capability (some kernels and KV-cache strategies scale better), tokenizer differences for multilingual, and tool-calling / structured output support. For 100k context we recommend models that Redwood has verified at long-context with chunked KV caching and quantization profiles. We can run benchmarks with your prompt set.
[01:48] Priya: Are there open models that actually handle 100k without huge latency penalties?
[01:52] Diego: Practically, yes — with the right runtime kernels and batching. We often use custom-compiled attention and streaming KV cache so you don't re-compute prefix tokens. But note there's a latency vs cost tradeoff; Dedicated with pinned GPUs helps. Hosted can do it too but you may see slightly higher variance during peaks.
[02:08] Liam: For multilingual: which model families are stronger? Our languages include Japanese and German which are pain points.
[02:14] Diego: Models trained on multilingual corpora — some Mistral-ish and XLM-style variants — perform better. Also the tokenizer and pretraining data matter. We run per-language evals and can surface bleed-through differences. We saw Cohere-ish families are decent on EN/ES but lag on JP; Llama-derivatives vary a lot depending on tokenization.
[02:33] Priya: Tool-calling: we need the model to call internal search API and then re-rank hits; tooling needs secure credentials and ephemeral access. How do you handle that?
[02:40] Diego: We have function/tool calling APIs and structured output support. For Dedicated/Private you can have the tool adapters run inside your VPC with secure IAM. Hosted also supports signed ephemeral tokens and network egress controls — but if you need full control over keys and no traffic leaving your network, Private is the path.
[02:57] Sara: Regarding audit and KMS: does Redwood support HSM-backed KMS and per-request audit logs?
[03:02] Maya: Yes — we integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated and Private, and provide audit logs and request-level tracing in the Console. We'll share the security packet (SOC 2, ISO) after the call.
[03:12] Priya: Great. Pricing talk — is there an estimated TCO for running high-context workloads?
[03:18] Maya: We usually prepare a TCO comparing Hosted variable usage vs Dedicated reserved capacity. For 100k context, Dedicated with optimized kernels and quantized models often lowers per-token costs if you have steady load. We'll send a sample spreadsheet.
[03:28] Liam: Any caveats around quantization accuracy for multilingual text? We worry about hallucination increases after aggressive quant.
[03:34] Diego: Absolutely — quantization can affect output quality, especially on tails and some languages. Our recommendation: run an eval set per language and per quant profile. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles based on your evals.
[03:46] Priya: Do you do tool chaining — like model calls external search, then model re-synthesizes with the search results?
[03:51] Diego: Yes, that's supported. We also support tool-call routing policies and retry/fallback. For sensitive data, you can enforce on-host tool adapters in Private/Dedicated so search results never leave your VPC.
[04:03] Sara: Data residency: we need logs to be retained on-region and only accessible to certain roles. RBAC?
[04:08] Maya: Console supports RBAC and audit retention policies. For Hosted we have region controls and per-customer retention; for Dedicated/Private you get stronger isolation and can manage retention in your infra.
[04:19] Priya: Ok good. Can you talk about latency expectations specifically for a 100k summarize job — like end-to-end from client to final chunked output?
[04:25] Diego: It's workload dependent but ballpark: chunking and KV streaming means you won't re-run attention for the entire context each token. For a single large summarize it might be in the 8-20s range depending on GPU config and batch size. If you need sub-5s, we often break the work into rolling summaries or pre-indexing; or use a Dedicated larger memory instance to keep more of the KV on device. We'll test with your exact prompts.
[04:47] Liam: That aligns with our experiments. We sometimes see 30s on naive runs.
[04:51] Priya: For pilot: what would you need from us?
[04:54] Maya: Sample prompt set, representative docs (anonymized), target languages, success metrics (latency SLOs, quality thresholds), and a short list of connectors/tools you want to call. Also which deployment mode you prefer for pilot (Hosted easiest, Dedicated for realistic perf, Private if compliance requires it).
[05:12] Priya: We'll prefer Dedicated for pilot to get realistic perf numbers, but might start with Hosted for a quick smoke.
[05:17] Maya: Sounds good. Any competitor lock-in concerns?
[05:20] Liam: We're worried about vendor-specific APIs for tool calling. We want the ability to migrate.
[05:24] Diego: Our APIs are standard REST/SDK; tooling and function schemas are portable. We also provide model-agnostic ligatures — sorry, nup, I meant abstractions — you can swap model variants with minimal code changes.
[05:34] Priya: One more security: SSO/SAML integration timelines?
[05:37] Maya: We support SAML/SSO and SCIM; for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your IdP during the pilot. We'll share the integration doc.
[05:45] Sara: Will you provide a data flow diagram and third-party subprocessors list?
[05:49] Maya: Yes, will include in the security pack.
[05:52] Diego: Quick note on mis-transcribes — sometimes our auto-transcripts say "KV cash" or stuff; ignore that, it's KV cache.
[05:58] Priya: (laughs) noted.
[06:00] Maya: OK wrapping — recap and next steps?
[06:02] Priya: Recap: we'll share prompt set + requirements, preference for Dedicated pilot but might smoke test on Hosted, need SOC2 docs and KMS/HSM details. Pilot timeline: kick off next week, results in ~1.5 weeks to two weeks, follow-up to review.
[06:16] Maya: Perfect. We'll: 1) send pricing + Hosted vs Dedicated TCO spreadsheet, 2) share security packet (SOC2/ISO/KMS/processor list), 3) Diego will schedule bench (100k context + multilingual), 4) set follow-up week of 2026-05-27.
